# Engineering practices {#sec-practices}

QViz was built as a hackathon project, but it follows the habits of a maintained
codebase. This page lists those habits. For each one, the rule is stated, the place
where it can be seen in the code is named, and the reason is given. The mechanical
style rules (imports, docstrings, line length) are on
[Style and conventions](../development/style-and-conventions.qmd).

## Design {.unnumbered}

### One responsibility per module {.unnumbered}

Each pipeline stage does one thing and returns a new type. The translator knows
nothing about simulation, and the simulator knows nothing about fidelity. A new
metric is added in `metrics` and nowhere else.

*Why.* A reader can open one file and understand one idea. A bug is located by
asking which stage produced the first wrong object.

### Modules do not import each other {.unnumbered}

Only `compiler` imports the stages. The others import `model`, `errors`, `config`,
`constants`, and, when a conversion is needed, `to_qiskit`. The full table is on
[Project structure](project-structure.qmd).

*Why.* There are no hidden dependencies and no cycles. A stage is tested with an
object made by hand, as the tests of `simulator` and `vectorizer` do.

### Orchestration is separate from logic {.unnumbered}

The whole `compiler` module is 71 lines. `compile` validates the arguments, calls the stages in order and
returns the result. It contains no physics. The decisions that look like logic
(the unsupported provider, the tomography branch) are the choice of which stage to
call, which is the job of an orchestrator.

*Why.* The order of the pipeline is readable in one screen. Changing it never
means searching for scattered calls.

### Immutable data, pure functions {.unnumbered}

Every object that crosses a stage boundary is a `@dataclass(frozen=True)` defined
in `model.py`, and tuples are used instead of lists. The public functions return
new objects and do not touch their input. There is no module-level state.

*Why.* Purity makes the functions deterministic, so they are easy to test and safe
to call twice. Immutability turns an accidental write into an exception at the
moment it happens, rather than a wrong number several stages later.

### Make illegal states hard to express {.unnumbered}

Names such as the entangler and the gate are `Literal` types (`"ms" | "zz"`,
`"gpi" | "gpi2" | "ms" | "zz" | "virtual_z"`). The functions that dispatch on a
gate end with `assert_never`, in `simulator._matrix` and in `to_qiskit`.

*Why.* If a new gate is added to the type and a function forgets it, `assert_never`
raises at once (and a type checker would flag it before that), instead of the
function silently skipping the gate.

### Constants and configuration are different things {.unnumbered}

`constants.py` holds values that are part of the definition (a full turn in
radians). `config.py` holds values that are a policy (`MAX_QUBITS`, the number of
decimals of the JSON, the timeout of the IonQ job). Each configuration value has a
docstring that says why it has that number.

*Why.* A maintainer who wants to change a limit finds it in one place, and knows
that it is safe. Nobody changes a constant by mistake.

## Correctness {.unnumbered}

### Test against an independent oracle {.unnumbered}

A test that compares code with a copy of itself proves little. The suite uses
Qiskit as the reference instead.

| What is checked | Oracle |
| --- | --- |
| The translation is correct | `Operator(source).equiv(Operator(to_qiskit(native)))` |
| The simulation is correct | `Statevector` and `partial_trace` of Qiskit |
| The JSON is valid | `documentation/schema/visualization.schema.json`, with `jsonschema` |
| The JSON has not drifted | A golden file, `source/tests/golden/bell_basic.json` |

When the documentation of IonQ and its own matrices disagreed, the matrices and the
tests were taken as the authority. This is recorded in
`documentation/references/ionq_native_gates.md`.

### Tolerances are honest {.unnumbered}

Numerical comparisons use `atol=1e-9`. A failing test is fixed at its cause; the
tolerance is not loosened to make it pass. The statistical tests of the tomography use a looser tolerance, and the sampler
tests pass a fixed `seed`, so a failure can be repeated.

### Validate at the boundary {.unnumbered}

Data that comes from outside is checked where it enters. `compile` rejects an
unknown strategy or a non-positive number of shots before it touches the transpiler,
so a typo cannot spend the single IonQ job of a run. `sample` receives a JSON that a
web page may have modified, so it checks every field (finite numbers, valid targets,
one value per qubit) and raises a `QVizError` that names the step and the reason.

*Why.* Inside the library, the data is trusted. At the edge, it is not.

### Fail with a precise error {.unnumbered}

Every error is an instance of `QVizError` or one of its subclasses
(`UnsupportedOperationError`, `CircuitTooLargeError`, `UnsupportedProviderError`,
`CircuitParseError`, `TranspilationError`). Messages say what was found and what is
accepted, for example `entangler must be 'auto', 'ms' or 'zz', got 'foo'`. A bad
value is never replaced silently by a default. Where the library catches a broad
`Exception` to fall back, the line carries a comment that says why.

### Never fail where classification is enough {.unnumbered}

`provider.detect` does not raise. A backend that is neither IonQ nor the built-in
simulator is classified as `unsupported`, and `compile` decides what to do about
it. The detection answers a question; the policy is somewhere else.

## Safety and cost {.unnumbered}

- **One IonQ job per run.** The rule comes from Qollab. `compile` makes at most one
  `backend.run`, and `allow_remote=False` makes none.
- **No paid hardware by accident.** The tomography sends many circuits, so it
  refuses a hardware backend unless `allow_paid=True` is passed.
- **No secrets.** There are no API keys or tokens in the repository, because the
  published code is public.
- **Dependencies are checked.** Each one has a permissive license (MIT, BSD,
  Apache-2.0, ISC), and it is recorded in the specification. `requirements.txt` must
  equal the dependencies of `pyproject.toml`, and a test compares them.

## Maintainability {.unnumbered}

### Logging, not printing {.unnumbered}

Inside `source/backend/core`, messages go through
`logging.getLogger(__name__)`. A caller decides whether to see them. `print` is used
only in `main.py` and in the scripts.

### Write the specification first {.unnumbered}

`documentation/internal/spec.md` defines the architecture, the units, the JSON
contract and a plan by module. A module is built against its section, with its tests
and a demo, and it is marked *ready to validate* only when `make test` and the demo
pass. When the code shows that the specification is wrong, both are corrected in
the same change.

### One module at a time, with a stop {.unnumbered}

The work proceeds in the order M0 to M10. After each module the author stops and
reports what was done, how to validate it and what remains unverified on Qollab.
The next module starts after the team agrees.

*Why.* A pipeline fails far from its cause. Validating each stage before building
the next keeps the failures local.

### Document where the knowledge is lost {.unnumbered}

Three kinds of knowledge would otherwise be forgotten, and each has a home.

| Knowledge | Where it lives |
| --- | --- |
| Why a decision was made | The specification, and the decision notes in `documentation/internal/`. |
| What is true about Qollab | `qollab.qmd` and the test table in `documentation/internal/qollab_pruebas.md`, with the date of each measurement. |
| Where the project stands | `memory.md`, kept under 150 lines by a test. |

### Units are stated, always {.unnumbered}

An angle is radians or turns, and the unit is part of the name or the docstring.
`qiskit-ionq` uses turns for the entangling angle; the conversion happens at the
border, once. See [Units and conventions](../concepts/units-and-conventions.qmd).

## Delivery {.unnumbered}

- **Continuous integration** runs the linters, the JavaScript syntax check, the
  Qollab package build, the tests (Python 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14) and the Quarto book
  render on every push and pull request.
- **Branches** follow a simple flow: `main` is stable, `development` integrates, and
  one `feature/<module>` branch per module. The commands are in `Makefile.git`.
- **Commits** are made when the team asks, in English, with a short first line.
  Hooks are never skipped and history is never rewritten on shared branches.
- **Generated folders are not edited.** `qollab/` is rebuilt by `make qollab`, and
  `out/` by `make outputs`.

## Practices in the viewer {.unnumbered}

The same ideas apply to the JavaScript, with the limits of the platform in mind.

- **State in one place.** `js/state.js` holds all the mutable state of the viewer.
  No value hides in the document or in a closure.
- **Optional hooks with a fallback.** Everything Qollab adds is read as
  `HOST.<name>` and has a default. The viewer runs without Qollab.
- **A test per risk of the platform.** The packager has tests for each thing Qollab
  broke: the 100-file limit, the missing `main.py`, import cycles in the bundled
  modules, and the services that the prelude defines but the viewer does not read.
- **Accessibility is a feature, not an afterthought.** The *View and accessibility*
  panel offers profiles (focus, high contrast, colour-blind palettes, reduced
  motion), camera buttons for people who do not use a keyboard, and an `aria-live`
  announcement of each step.
- **Bilingual interface.** Texts are chosen with `t(es, en)` according to
  `<html lang>`.

## Known limits {.unnumbered}

These limits are known and still open.

- The viewer has no automated browser test. It is checked by hand, and by headless
  Chromium for the bundle, and its modules are exercised with a stub DOM.
- The tomography with `qiskit-ionq` older than 1.0.3 fails on backends that are
  not IonQ, because the native gates carry no definition.
- The comparison of the tomography with the exact statevector is not implemented;
  the circuit is compiled twice.
- Only IonQ and the built-in simulator are supported. IBM and AWS backends are
  rejected on purpose. See the [Compiler](../modules/compiler.qmd).
